transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… the main thing is at work. I’m a nurse, and on the floor I keep losing my train of thought. Like I’ll be in the middle of figuring out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump starts beeping, or someone asks another nurse something nearby, or a call light goes off, and suddenly it’s just… gone. I’m standing there trying to remember what I was just doing.

And it’s frustrating because hospitals are always noisy, obviously — I mean, that’s the job, right? There’s always something happening. But it feels like my brain just gets pulled away constantly, and then I’m trying to pick the thread back up. That’s really what brought me in.
Have you noticed this kind of distractibility and trouble staying on task for as long as you can remember, even back in school, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, I think it goes way back. Like, even in elementary school, my teachers would write on report cards that I was bright but careless—those exact kinds of comments. I was always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework, even when I’d done it.

My mom had to sit with me pretty much every night to keep me on track, like at the kitchen table, and she’d be reminding me what I was supposed to be doing. I remember the smell of those little pencil shavings from the sharpener—sorry, that’s random—but yeah, it wasn’t just a recent work thing. It’s been there since I was a kid.
Growing up and now, have you also struggled with feeling restless, needing to move around, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Yeah… I don’t know if I’d call myself physically restless exactly, but the talking thing, yes. Like during handoff, or if I’m mentoring a newer nurse, I’ll mean to just give the important points, and then I’m somehow giving the whole backstory and circling around.

I’ll notice people kind of looking at the clock or trying to jump in, and I’m still like, “Oh wait, one more thing,” and I can’t seem to wrap it up neatly. It’s embarrassing because I know everyone’s busy, and then I’m thinking, okay, why did I say all that?
Do you often find yourself interrupting or blurting things out before someone finishes speaking, or making quick decisions—like in patient care or elsewhere—without fully thinking them through first?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I make quick patient-care decisions without thinking, at least not in a way I’ve noticed. If anything, I can get kind of stuck trying to make sure I’m not missing something.

With interrupting, maybe sometimes? Like I might jump in if I think I know where someone’s going, but I don’t know if that’s a big pattern or just normal conversation stuff. Sorry, I’m thinking of handoff again—there was this one time someone was explaining a discharge plan and I had like three questions in my head, and then I was trying to remember them before they disappeared, but… I don’t know. I guess I’m not sure how often it actually happens.
Do you often feel physically restless or fidgety—like needing to tap your foot, get up and move around, or feeling like you can't sit still for long periods, even outside of work?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who can’t sit still, like I’m not pacing around all the time or anything.

I mean, at work I’m moving constantly anyway, so it’s hard to tell. Outside of work… I guess if I’m sitting for a long movie or something, I might shift around, but I feel like everybody does that? Sorry, I’m thinking of this one movie my friend made me see that was almost three hours, and I kept checking the time—but that might’ve just been the movie.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed physical restlessness as a big thing.
Outside of work, do you notice yourself making impulsive decisions—like spending money quickly, blurting things out in conversations with friends or family, or acting before thinking things through?

I’m not sure. I mean, with money, I don’t think I’m like… going out and buying huge things on a whim or anything. I’ll buy random little stuff sometimes, but then I feel like everyone does that, especially online when it’s like “only two left” or whatever—actually that happened with some storage bins the other day, which sounds ridiculous now.

With conversations, I might say something too quickly sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it blurting. My family would probably have a more honest answer than me, honestly. I don’t really think of myself as someone who acts without thinking, though. I usually overthink if anything.
Do you often feel mentally 'revved up' or restless on the inside—like your mind is racing or you have trouble relaxing and slowing down—even when you're sitting still?

I’m not sure. I don’t know if I’d describe it as “revved up,” exactly. Like, I can sit still, and I don’t feel like I’m buzzing or anything.

My mind does jump around sometimes, but then I start thinking, well, maybe that’s just because there’s always a lot going on—like I’ll be sitting at home and remember I need to text someone back, then wonder if I paid a bill, then think about something totally unrelated like what groceries I forgot. Actually I forgot eggs twice last week, which is annoying because I had the carton in my hand at one point and then put it back for some reason—

Sorry. What was the wording? Trouble relaxing? I guess I haven’t really noticed that as a constant thing. I wouldn’t confidently say yes.
Do you often find it hard to wait your turn—like in lines, in traffic, or waiting for someone to finish a thought before you respond?

I’m not sure. Lines are annoying, but I don’t know if I’m worse than other people. Like at the grocery store I’ll pick the line that looks shortest and then immediately regret it when someone has coupons or there’s a price check—sorry, that sounds so petty. I mostly just stand there and get irritated in my head.

In traffic, same thing, I guess. I don’t love it, but I’m not like honking constantly or trying to cut people off.

Waiting for someone to finish talking… maybe sometimes I’m thinking of what I want to say, but I don’t know if that’s “can’t wait my turn” or just normal conversation. So I wouldn’t say that’s a big thing I’ve noticed.
Have you been feeling particularly anxious, worried, or down lately, in a way that might be making it hard to concentrate?

I’m not sure. I mean, I get stressed, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious or down in a specific way. Work can be a lot, and then I come home and there’s laundry or dishes or I realize I forgot to move something from the washer—actually that happened yesterday and now the towels smell weird, which is… sorry, not really what you asked.

I guess I haven’t noticed my mood being the main reason I can’t focus. Like, I’m not sitting there thinking, “I’m too sad to concentrate,” if that makes sense. Worried sometimes, sure, but I don’t know if it’s particular or more than normal.
